name: Lorenzo McMullen Jr.
strengths: McMullen creates clear cushions on vertical routes — defenders struggle to stay stride-for-stride at 6-2.
McMullen tracks the ball through traffic and wins with length at the catch point.
McMullen turns separation into yards after the catch with long strides into the second level.
weaknesses: McMullen still needs to add mass to his 170-pound frame to play through SEC press every down.
comparison: McMullen comps to Justin Jefferson — 6-1 / 6-2 separator with length, clean tracking, and the ability to win vertically and after the catch.
projection: McMullen projects as a Year 2 SEC starter at WR (packages Year 1). Ceiling: All-SEC playmaker — the elite vertical separator who can become Florida’s every-down perimeter hammer.
schemeFit: McMullen fits as a perimeter X/Z who can win vertically and grow into every-down snaps as the frame fills.
insiderNotes: McMullen is a top-shelf 6-2 / 170 Princeton (Ohio) WR who creates vertical cushions, tracks cleanly, and strides away after the catch. Wins with separation and length — an elite board WR who can stress any coverage Florida faces.
